issue: Does a plea agreement's appeal waiver covering any sentence imposed bar a claim that the written judgment conflicts with the oral sentence?

sides.position: A challenge to a conflict between the written judgment and the oral sentence falls within a waiver of the right to appeal 'any sentence imposed,' because both pronouncements qualify as the sentence.
cases: United States v. Higgins, 739 F.3d 733 (5th Cir. 2014)

sides.position: A challenge to a conflict between the written judgment and the oral sentence does not fall within a waiver of the right to appeal 'any sentence imposed.'
cases: United States v. Singletary, 984 F.3d 341 (4th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Harris, 51 F.4th 705 (7th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Shaw, 139 F.4th 548 (6th Cir. 2025)

this_court: The majority agrees with the Fourth and Seventh Circuits that such a challenge is not barred by the waiver, and it rejects the claim on the merits.
quote: Yet the Fourth and Seventh Circuits have since disagreed.
cite: United States v. Tracey Shaw, 139 F.4th 548 (6th Cir. 2025)
